title: Grade 4 ELA — Figurative Language in Context
subject: English Language Arts
description: Practice with questions on simile, metaphor, personification, idioms.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: “The classroom was a beehive before the show.” What does that suggest?
choices: There was a swarm of real bees.

questions.question: “Her voice was as soft as falling snow.” What is being compared?
“The wind whispered through the curtains.” What human action is given to wind?
What does “break the ice” mean when someone tells a joke to a quiet group?
“Milo zipped past like a rocket.” What does the simile stress?
“Stars winked at us” gives stars a human action. What is this technique?
Which sentence contains a simile?
choices: The mud felt like thick glue.
The mud was on my boots.
The mud dried in the sun.

questions.question: Which is a metaphor?
choices: The test was ten questions long.
I took the test after lunch.
The test was as long as a movie.

questions.question: What does “lend a hand” mean in “Can you lend a hand with the boxes?”
choices: write your name on the box

questions.question: “The old house groaned in the wind.” What real sound does the writer likely describe?
“I've told you a million times” is likely meant to show what?
choices: the speaker has said it often
the speaker kept an exact count

questions.question: “He felt under the weather.” What does the idiom mean?
“Time crawled while we waited.” What did waiting feel like?
“Her grin was a flashlight in a dark room.” What does that suggest about her grin?
choices: It lit the room with a bulb.

questions.question: Which sentence uses “sharp” figuratively?
choices: The knife has a sharp edge.

questions.question: Which sentence gives a thing a human action?
choices: The river flowed past the bank.

questions.question: What would “on the same page” mean during a team project?
choices: writing in the same notebook only

questions.question: Which detail acts as a comparison with “as”?
choices: His feet were as cold as ice.
He stepped away from the ice.

questions.question: “The news hit me like cold water.” What feeling does the comparison suggest?
“The trail ribboned across the valley.” What did the trail likely look like?
